analysis.title: UBS Seasonality Insights: Squeeze Risk
key_insights: November is the best month of the year for the S&P 500, averaging +1.9% since 1950. Only one negative November in the last 10 years (2021). Halloween starts the six-month 'Buy in November' stretch, the counterpart to 'Sell in May'.

The positive seasonal coincides with a short squeeze risk. Net exposure is very low while gross exposure is at multi-year highs because shorts have risen sharply. UBS outlines four seasonal catalysts that could drive a squeeze and a broader year-end performance chase.

A Blue Sweep is the base case for the midterms. The size of Democratic gains and key Senate and gubernatorial races (e.g. Texas) remain unknowns into next week. Unwinding of election uncertainty has historically produced strong forward equity returns at high hit rates, and the S&P has been higher six months after election day for every midterm since 1950.

November is the weakest month for oil, down 2.9% on average. Copper has its best month of the year (+1.7%). UBS says Iran-related tail risks remain fat in both escalation and de-escalation directions. If oil declines, swapping Energy equity exposure into Metals & Mining {UBXXMETL} looks compelling.

The VIX sees its biggest decline of the year in November. The MOVE Index sees its second weakest month of the year, and given recently elevated rates volatility, a further decline would be a tailwind for equities.

November is the weakest month for US 10y yields. The ~30bps retracement to ~5% has already supported Housing {UBXXHOME} and Bond Proxies {UBXXBOND}. Lower yields driven by energy disinflation are bullish for the broad index, while lower yields driven by weaker AI growth assumptions are not.
